true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition overrides the width/height version

OptimizedImage now defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) and again at line 149 as downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}). In Ruby the later definition replaces the earlier one, so any existing caller passing separate width and height arguments will raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), and the line-145 implementation is dead code. The width/height API must be kept working or all callers updated/removed deliberately.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side upload limit hardcoded to 10MB ignores site settings and upload type

validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], respecting different configured limits for images vs attachments. It now hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 for every file type. Sites with a lower max_attachment_size_kb/max_image_size_kb will let users select files the server will reject, and sites configured above 10MB will incorrectly block uploads they intend to allow. The same regression is repeated in displayErrorForUpload at line 246, which reports 10MB as the limit on a 413 response regardless of the actual configured/server limit.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage downsize breaks animated GIF handling

The controller calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails). When allow_animation is true and the file is a GIF, OptimizedImage.optimize dispatches to downsize_instructions_animated/resize_instructions_animated, which passes the dimensions to gifsicle as --resize-fit. Gifsicle expects WxH dimensions, not "80%" (the value also gets a trailing \> from the non-animated path conventions), so it will fail to resize animated GIFs. The loop then retries the failing operation up to 5 times and the oversized GIF proceeds to Upload.create_for still over the limit, so large animated uploads are not actually downsized.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsize failures are ignored and the same file is used as input and output

The resizing loop ignores the boolean return value of OptimizedImage.downsize and uses tempfile.path as both source and destination. If convert/gifsicle fails (corrupt image, unsupported format such as SVG, unsupported geometry), convert_with returns false but the loop still runs up to 5 expensive attempts and then uploads whatever is left at that path. Using the same path for input and output also risks truncating/corrupting the only copy of the uploaded tempfile if the external tool fails part-way, and for non-animated GIFs the [0] selector in downsize_instructions silently reduces the image to its first frame. Failures should be checked and the resize should go through a separate temporary output file that replaces the original only on success.

Remote download limit hardcoded to 10MB bypasses configured image limit before validation

FileHelper.download for API-provided URLs previously capped the download at SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes; it now always allows 10.megabytes. Combined with the new in-request downsizing, an API caller can force the server to download and run up to 5 ImageMagick/ImageOptim passes over a 10MB untrusted image even on sites whose configured max_image_size_kb is much smaller, increasing bandwidth/CPU (decompression-bomb) exposure. If the image still exceeds max_image_size_kb after 5 attempts it is only then rejected by normal upload validation, after the expensive work has been done.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes when host is nil

The before_validation block calls self.host.sub! without checking for nil, and there is no presence validation evaluated before this callback. Creating a host with a missing host parameter (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host], which is nil when the key is absent) raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation and returning a JSON error, producing a 500.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update and destroy crash with a 500 for a nonexistent host id

Both update and destroy use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately call save_host(host) or host.destroy without a nil check. A stale admin UI (e.g. a host deleted in another tab) or a hand-crafted request with an unknown id therefore raises NoMethodError on nil instead of returning a 404. save_host also dereferences params[:embeddable_host] without checking its presence, with the same 500-on-malformed-request problem.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration interpolates stored host values directly into SQL and stores them unsanitized

Each line from the old embeddable_hosts setting is interpolated unescaped into an INSERT statement ('#{h}'). A host value containing a single quote breaks the migration, and a crafted value can inject arbitrary SQL executed with the migration's privileges. Additionally the raw value is stored verbatim, so legacy entries like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (both valid in the old setting) are stored with scheme/path intact; EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares them against URI(host).host, which never equals such a string, so those hosts silently stop being allowed after migration. The values should be inserted with quoting/bound parameters and normalized the same way the model normalizes them (strip scheme and path).

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files

category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the newly added embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category). Fabrication loads every file so tests still pass, but the swapped contents are misleading for future maintainers editing or adding fabricators, and any tooling that loads fabricator files selectively by name will register the wrong definitions. The contents should be moved back into their eponymous files.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration interpolates stored host values directly into SQL and stores them unsanitized

Each line from the old embeddable_hosts setting is interpolated unescaped into an INSERT statement ('#{h}'). A host value containing a single quote breaks the migration, and a crafted value can inject arbitrary SQL executed with the migration's privileges. Additionally the raw value is stored verbatim, so legacy entries like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (both valid in the old setting) are stored with scheme/path intact; EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares them against URI(host).host, which never equals such a string, so those hosts silently stop being allowed after migration. The values should be inserted with quoting/bound parameters and normalized the same way the model normalizes them (strip scheme and path).

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category is not set in the database

The migration unconditionally does execute(...)[0]['id'] for the embed_category lookup. On a fresh install, or any site that never changed embed_category (site_settings only stores non-default values), that query returns zero rows, so [0] is nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and leaving the upgrade half-applied. The same pattern on line 15 for uncategorized_category_id has the same problem. The lookup needs to handle an empty result before indexing into it.

false_negatives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

false_positives.candidate:
Duplicate and case-variant hosts are allowed, making category selection nondeterministic

There is no uniqueness validation on host. An admin can create two embeddable_hosts rows for the same hostname (including case variants, since stored case is preserved and matching lowercases only the column side) pointing at different categories. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host then returns .first with no ORDER BY, so which category embedded topics land in, and effectively which row governs the host, is arbitrary database order. A case-insensitive uniqueness validation (and matching index) is needed.

Edit action crashes when a host has no resolvable category

The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') unconditionally. host.category is only populated by the store's embedded hydration via Discourse.Category.findById(category_id); if the referenced category was deleted or is not among the site's loaded categories, category is undefined and clicking edit throws a TypeError, making the row impossible to edit or fix from the UI. The same assumption appears on save (line 38), where a blank categoryId sets host.category to undefined even though the server silently substitutes the uncategorized category, so the row displays no category until reload.

Host validation permits ports and rejects long TLDs, inconsistent with host matching

The format regex explicitly allows a port (':[0-9]{1,5}') and paths, but record_for_host matches against URI(referer).host, which excludes the port, so a validated host like 'example.com:3000' can never match and embedding from it is always rejected. Conversely the regex limits the TLD to 2-5 letters, so legitimate hosts on newer/longer TLDs (e.g. .technology, .international) cannot be added at all. The accepted format and the matching logic need to agree.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser record

TopicUser.find_by can return nil for users who receive a topic email without ever having visited/interacted with the topic (e.g. category watchers notified of a new topic, or mentioned/quoted users). The next line calls tu.notification_level on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. Use a creating/upserting API such as TopicUser.change instead of assuming a row exists.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping

Assigning notification_level and calling tu.save! skips the logic in TopicUser.change that stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, observes after-save callbacks, and publishes a MessageBus notification_level_change. Other open clients therefore keep showing the old notification state and the change is not recorded consistently with every other notification-level change in the app. Call TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) instead.

First click does not actually stop notifications for watching/tracking users

If notification_level is above regular (watching or tracking), the action only downgrades it to regular, not muted. A regular user still receives mention/quote/reply notifications for the topic, so the email promise 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and the landing page text 'You will stop receiving notifications' are false after the click the email invites; the user must discover and operate the extra dropdown to finish unsubscribing.

No test covers the new unsubscribe behaviour end-to-end

The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url to an existing MessageBuilder fixture, but the examples still assert only the user-preferences URL and List-Unsubscribe header; nothing asserts the per-topic URL actually appears in text/HTML bodies, and there is no controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all (level transitions watching->?, regular->muted, missing TopicUser row, wrong slug redirect, logged-out user). The nil-row crash and downgrade semantics above would not be caught by the test suite.

State-changing unsubscribe is an unauthenticated-by-token GET request GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe immediately mutates the currently logged-in user's notification level, with no signed per-recipient token and no confirmation step. Email link scanners/prefetchers will trigger it automatically, anyone the email is forwarded to who is logged in will change their own settings instead of the recipient's, and an attacker can embed the (predictable, enumerable topic id) URL in an on an external page to silently downgrade/mute a logged-in victim's topic notifications (CSRF on a GET, with check_xhr skipped). Unsubscribe links should carry a signed key identifying the recipient, and/or require a non-GET confirmation.

unsubscribe_link translation now hard-requires unsubscribe_url for every sender

The shared unsubscribe_link string now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, and Email::MessageBuilder passes template_args to I18n.t whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true (in both body and html_part). I18n raises MissingInterpolationArgument when a key is absent, so any current or plugin mailer that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without also passing unsubscribe_url (previously a valid, working combination) will now crash while building email. Only include the per-topic sentence when unsubscribe_url is present, or supply a default in MessageBuilder.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
should_block? uses a non-atomic read-modify-write inside a validator

should_block? increments match_count with `record.match_count += 1` followed by `save`. It is called from EmailValidator during ordinary model validation, so a single signup attempt that calls user.valid? and then user.save runs it at least twice and double-counts one attempt, and two concurrent attempts can read the same match_count and overwrite each other, losing counts. The write also makes validation itself have a database side effect that can fail or participate unexpectedly in surrounding transactions. Use an atomic SQL increment (e.g. update_counters/increment_counter with update for last_match_at) and ideally move the stat update out of the pure predicate/validator path so one rejected attempt is counted once.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup can be bypassed by changing letter case

should_block? performs an exact, case-sensitive database lookup for the supplied email, and neither BlockedEmail nor User normalizes email addresses to lowercase before saving or validation. An address stored as blocked@example.com therefore will not match a signup attempt using Blocked@Example.com or BLOCKED@example.com, allowing a trivial bypass of the block list (PostgreSQL string equality and the unique index are case-sensitive). Normalize addresses (downcase/strip) on both BlockedEmail save and lookup, or use a case-insensitive comparison.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
rejectedEmails is a shared prototype array that is never cleared

rejectedEmails is defined as Em.A([]) directly on the controller class prototype, so the same mutable array is shared by controller instances, and createAccount only ever pushObject()s into it. Once an email is rejected it stays rejected for the life of the page session even if the server-side reason disappears (address unblocked, conflicting account removed, admin fixes the record), forcing a page reload before the user can retry that address. Initialize the array per controller instance and clear it when the modal/account flow is reset.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses reversed substring matching

The handler accepts a message when discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) is not -1, i.e. when the sender origin is merely a substring of the configured Discourse URL string. Origin validation must be an exact origin comparison; substring matching accepts origins that are prefixes/substrings of the forum URL and is fragile with trailing slashes, ports, and look-alike hosts. A frame able to send a message from an accepted non-forum origin could resize the embed iframe unexpectedly.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Referer is interpolated unsafely and incorrectly as postMessage targetOrigin

The layout inserts the full user-controlled request.referer into a JavaScript string as the targetOrigin for parent.postMessage. A referer containing a quote or script-breaking sequence can break out of the string and execute attacker JavaScript in the embed page. Even for legitimate referers, a full URL such as http://host/post-path is not a valid targetOrigin (which must be an origin), so browsers may reject the message and the parent iframe will never receive the resize height.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
PollFeed crashes on feed items without a content element

The job unconditionally calls i.content.scrub and passes the result to CGI.unescapeHTML. Many RSS/Atom items expose only title/link/description or use a namespaced content field, so SimpleRSS can return nil for content. A single such item raises NoMethodError/TypeError and aborts the whole hourly poll, preventing all remaining items in that feed from being imported.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Referer is interpolated unsafely and incorrectly as postMessage targetOrigin

The layout inserts the full user-controlled request.referer into a JavaScript string as the targetOrigin for parent.postMessage. A referer containing a quote or script-breaking sequence can break out of the string and execute attacker JavaScript in the embed page. Even for legitimate referers, a full URL such as http://host/post-path is not a valid targetOrigin (which must be an origin), so browsers may reject the message and the parent iframe will never receive the resize height.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

false_positives.candidate:
Controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job

The success example stubs TopicRetriever.new and expects retrieve to be called, but EmbedController#best now calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and never references TopicRetriever directly. This example therefore fails against the implementation it ships with, and it leaves the actual enqueue arguments and loading-template behaviour unverified. The adjacent TopicView example also stubs TopicView.new to return nil, after which best.html.erb dereferences @topic_view.posts, so the success-path rendering is not genuinely exercised.

Disqus import silently drops the category option and now requires fetching each source URL

The thor command removes the documented -c/--category option, so existing import invocations passing it will now fail as an unknown switch. It also replaces local creation of the opening post from the Disqus export with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...), which performs an HTTP fetch and readability extraction for every thread; threads whose link is blank, offline, blocked, or no longer readable produce no opening post and their Disqus replies are skipped entirely, whereas previously they were imported from the export file alone.

Embed view does not check whether the viewer can see the topic

When a TopicEmbed exists, the controller builds a TopicView for that topic id and the embed template outputs raw post.cooked for its best posts. There is no guardian/can-see check comparable to the normal topic controller. If an originally public imported topic is later moved into a restricted category, made invisible, or otherwise access-controlled, anonymous visitors framing the embed from the allowed host can still read its best posts through /embed/best.

TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-create race on embed_url

Import first queries TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and only later creates the row inside a block, while the migration adds a unique index on embed_url. Two concurrent retrievals or feed polls for the same new URL can both see no embed, both create topics/posts, and then one fails with RecordNotUnique on TopicEmbed.create!, rolling back or orphaning work after external effects/jobs have been enqueued. Concurrent imports for the same URL should be serialized or the uniqueness violation handled as an update.

Untrusted feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization

TopicEmbed.import passes feed or remotely fetched HTML directly to PostCreator with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns that raw value as cooked. PollFeed supplies RSS/Atom content with no HTML sanitization, and the normal post rendering path trusts cooked HTML. A malicious or compromised feed item containing a script event handler or other active markup can therefore be stored and executed in the browsers of users viewing the resulting topic, not only in the embed view.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin is off by one for legacy WebKit flexbox

The mixin emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val`, but the legacy box ordinal-group property is 1-based (its default is 1), whereas the standard `order` property is 0-based. The legacy value therefore needs to be `$val + 1`. As written, calls such as `@include order(2)` on .extra-info-wrapper and `@include order(3)` on .d-header .panel produce inconsistent ordering between legacy -webkit-box browsers and browsers using the standard `order` property, and an eventual `order(0)` or `order(1)` would collide with the default group. Fix the legacy declaration to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1` (and apply the same adjustment to -moz-box-ordinal-group).

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

false_positives.candidate:
Converting .small-action to flexbox silently disables the action button's float:right

Making .small-action a flex container (lines 264-265) makes its direct children flex items, and `float` has no effect on flex items. The nested `button` rule at lines 306-310 still relies on `float: right` to pin the small-action button to the right edge, but that declaration is now ignored and no flex replacement (e.g. `margin-left: auto` on the button) is provided. The button will instead sit immediately after .small-action-desc, changing the layout of small action posts. Add `margin-left: auto` (or equivalent flex positioning) to the button and remove the dead float.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the question mark and will never be called

Every other conditional inclusion hook in this serializer is named include_<attribute>? (e.g. include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?, include_stats?). The new hook is defined as include_website_name without the '?', so ActiveModel::Serializer will not use it to gate inclusion. website_name is therefore serialized even when website is blank, producing a website_name: nil key instead of omitting the attribute as intended.

false_positives.candidate:
Root domain versus www subdomain is not treated as the same domain

The same-domain check handles sibling subdomains of equal depth (www.example.com vs forum.example.com, lines 144-146) and a parent website domain (example.com vs forums.example.com, line 149), but not the common root/www pair: with Discourse at example.com and a website of http://www.example.com/user, the lengths differ (2 vs 3) so it falls to the else branch, example.com does not end with .www.example.com, and only www.example.com is returned without /user. The inverse direction works, so the displayed website name depends asymmetrically on which host carries the www prefix.

website_name discards query string and fragment from the website URL

When the website is on the instance domain, website_name is built as host + URI(website).path only. Any query string or fragment in the user's website (e.g. http://example.com/profile?tab=posts) is silently dropped from the displayed text, so the link label no longer shows the complete URL even though the stated purpose of the change is to show the complete URL path for same-domain websites.

website_name leaks websites that are hidden as untrusted attributes

website is listed in untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111), so it is hidden from anonymous viewers for TL0 users to prevent spam/abuse, but the newly added website_name attribute is not added to that list. An anonymous viewer of a TL0 profile therefore receives website_name, which is derived directly from the hidden website and reveals its host and, in the same-domain case, its full path, defeating the restriction and rendering the website link text even though website itself was withheld.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Light/dark lightness values swapped for embedded-post author link

The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)), so the light-theme value is changed from 30% to 70% and the dark-theme value is 30% instead of the complementary 70%. Both themes therefore get the opposite shade from the intended conversion, changing light-theme appearance and giving a too-dark colour on dark themes. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

true_positives.golden_comment: This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Group member name lightness changed from 30% to 50% in both themes

The original .group-member-info .name rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The change replaces it with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), altering the existing light-theme colour from 30% to 50% and using 50% rather than the complementary 70% for dark themes. Consistent with the rest of this PR it should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

true_positives.golden_comment: In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Light/dark lightness values swapped for .custom-message-length

Members endpoint accepts unbounded and invalid limit/offset values

limit and offset are taken directly from request parameters with only to_i conversion. A caller can request limit=1000000 to force loading and serializing an entire large group in one request, or supply negative values that can produce database errors. The server should clamp limit to a sane maximum and clamp both values to be non-negative instead of trusting the JavaScript client to do so.

The members endpoint now always applies limit/offset with a default limit of 50, whereas non-automatic groups previously returned all members. false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback loading is only wired into web requests

The PR is described as server-side localization fallbacks, but `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Server-side code that sets `I18n.locale` and translates without going through this controller (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, plugin background work) never loads the site-default/English fallback files, so with the lazy translation loader those fallbacks silently return missing translations there. The ensure-loaded step belongs in the shared translation path (e.g. `I18n.translate`/`load_locale` logic), not solely in a controller filter.

Fallback locales are not loaded before cached translation lookup

`translate` only loads `config.locale`, not the fallback locales configured in `FallbackLocaleList`. Outside `ApplicationController#set_locale` (background jobs, mailers, console, or translations before that filter) a key missing from the current locale will be looked up in fallback locales whose YAML files have never been loaded via the lazy-loading patch, so it returns a missing-translation string. Worse, the no-argument path stores that result in the LRU cache (`@cache.getset(k) { translate_no_cache(key).freeze }`), so the missing string stays cached under `key+locale` even after the fallback locale is later loaded, until eviction/reload. Fallbacks must be ensured-loaded inside `translate` (or the backend lookup) before computing/caching the value, and the cache must not persist results computed before fallback locales were loaded.

Fallback lookup queries SiteSetting on every translation

`FallbackLocaleList#[]` is called by the I18n fallbacks backend on every translation lookup, and it calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` each time. That puts a site-setting lookup (backed by Discourse's setting provider/cache machinery) on the hottest possible path — the very path `translate_accelerator.rb` exists to optimize — and it also raises `NoMethodError` if `default_locale` is ever nil/blank (e.g. early boot or a cleared setting). The fallback chain should be computed without a per-lookup setting query, or at minimum memoized/guarded with a safe default such as `:en`.

No tests cover the custom fallback chain or its lazy loading

This PR introduces a custom `FallbackLocaleList`, replaces the Rails `config.i18n.fallbacks` mechanism, removes the standalone pluralization initializer, and adds `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, but adds no specs. There is nothing verifying that a key missing in the user locale falls back to the site default and then English, that fallback locale files actually get loaded under the lazy-loading patch (including outside controllers), or that pluralized fallback strings still work. Regressions in this global I18n behavior would only surface as missing-translation strings in production; add specs for the fallback order, loading, and a pluralized fallback lookup before merging.

false_positives.candidate:
Insert-time eviction can silently drop the segment/root span and leaves has_root_span stale

When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, zpopmin evicts the lowest-scored (earliest end_timestamp_precise) members with no metric or log, silently discarding real span payloads rather than flagging the oversized segment as the previous flush-time check did. The evicted members can include the segment/root span (e.g. a short root span, clock skew, or a root whose children report later precise end times); the has_root_span flag computed just below still returns true because it is based on the stored flag or is_root_span of the current insert, so the now root-less segment is queued with the short root timeout and flushed as an incomplete segment. Buffer.py also removed the max_segment_spans guard in _load_segment_data (line 449), so there is no longer any flush-side detection of oversized segments produced by pre-change keys or any path that bypasses this eviction.

No test covers the new eviction, score-ordering, or paginator behavior

The test changes only add the now-required end_timestamp_precise field to existing Span constructions. Nothing exercises a segment growing past 1000 spans to verify zpopmin eviction keeps the intended (latest/root) spans, nothing verifies segments are ordered or deduplicated correctly after the SET-to-ZSET migration, and there are no tests at all for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized_pagination branch in the audit-log endpoint, which currently crash on datetime keys and negative offsets. The core behavioral change of this PR is therefore unverified.

Switching span sets from SET to ZSET breaks in-flight segments with WRONGTYPE errors

This changes the on-Redis type of span-buf:s:* keys from a Redis SET (sadd/sscan/scard/sunionstore) to a ZSET (zadd/zscan/zcard/zunionstore in buffer.py and add-buffer.lua) with no key versioning, draining, or dual-type handling. During a rolling deploy, keys created by old consumers are SETs; new code calling ZADD/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN on them returns WRONGTYPE, failing process_spans/flush for those traces, and old consumers similarly fail on new ZSET keys during rollback. Buffered keys live up to redis_ttl (3600s), so in-flight segments will error and can be dropped for up to an hour around deploys.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

Upsampling decision uses outer dataset and request query, not the scoped query actually executed

Consequently split error-only queries can fail to upsample while split transaction/other queries can be decided from the unrelated original request query, and the split has_errors/has_transactions comparisons can mix upsampled and non-upsampled results. Pass scoped_dataset and the effective query string into the decision.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Cached allowlist eligibility can go stale and be inconsistent within one request

Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds under a key built from hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))), but invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called from anywhere (option changes have no invalidation hook), so removing a project from the allowlist keeps upsampling its counts (and adding one delays it) with no bound tied to config changes. Additionally _get_event_stats re-evaluates this on every invocation, and the dashboard-split flow invokes it several times per request; a cache expiry mid-request can make the error, original, and transaction sub-queries disagree. Combined with hash() collisions between different project sets for the same organization, one set can also inherit another set's cached eligibility. Compute the decision once per request (or key the cache deterministically on the project IDs) instead of relying on an uninvalidated TTL cache.

Negated or quoted event.type:error incorrectly triggers upsampling

_is_error_focused_query does a raw substring check for 'event.type:error' on the lowercased query string. A query such as '!event.type:error' (explicitly excluding errors, e.g. transaction/default events) contains that substring and returns True, as would the text inside a quoted title/message value. The endpoint then rewrites count() to sum(sample_weight), which does not exist/apply for those non-error events, producing wrong (likely zero/NULL) counts. The query needs to be parsed (or at minimum negation/quoting handled) rather than substring-matched, and spaced forms like 'event.type: error' are also missed by the current check.

No tests for the public eligibility entry point, caching, or mixed sample_weight data

The new tests only cover the private helpers _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, _is_error_focused_query (happy paths), _should_apply_sample_weight_transform, and the column rewrite. is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects itself — including its 60s cache behaviour, the errors-vs-discover dataset gate combined with allowlist state, negated queries like '!event.type:error', and events in allowlisted projects that have no sample_weight/client_sample_rate — is never exercised at the unit level, and the Snuba tests only store events that all carry client_sample_rate=0.1. These are exactly the paths where counts can silently become 0 or be wrongly upsampled, so regression coverage should be added before merging.

Stray subproject file committed at repository root

This adds a file named 'sentry-repo' containing only 'Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a', which looks like an accidental git submodule/gitlink artifact rather than intended source. It should be removed before merge to avoid confusing tooling and repository layout.

upsampled_count is exposed as a public function for non-allowlisted projects

Unlike neighbouring internal aggregates, the new SnQLFunction 'upsampled_count' in discover.py is not marked private, and transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling emits it as a user-visible column string. Any user can therefore send yAxis=upsampled_count() directly for any project/dataset, bypassing the all-projects-allowlisted gate in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, and get sum(sample_weight) results (NULL/0 for projects without sampling) presented as legitimate counts. Mark the function private like the other internal-only aggregates so it can only be produced by the server-side rewrite.

upsampled_count undercounts events without sample_weight

upsampled_count computes toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce/fallback to 1 for rows where sample_weight is NULL. Allowlisted projects can contain events predating client error sampling, events from SDKs that do not send error_sampling context, or otherwise unsampled events; for those rows sum() ignores NULLs, so a bucket containing only such events returns NULL/0 instead of its real count and mixed buckets silently undercount. The transform in error_upsampling.py applies this to every count() for allowlisted projects, so historical/normal error events disappear from charts. Use a per-row fallback such as coalesce(sample_weight, 1) before summing.

false_positives.candidate:

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

If a user transcribes a valid code in uppercase (a-f become A-F), or an authenticator/backup note uppercases it, indexOf returns -1 and a valid single-use code is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode. The lookup should normalize the submitted code (e.g. trim and toLowerCase) before comparison.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Single-use backup codes can be replayed concurrently

Authorize reads user.backupCodes, checks indexOf, then later does a separate prisma.user.update setting backupCodes[index] = null. There is no atomic/conditional update or transaction locking the row between check and consumption. Two parallel login attempts using the same backup code can both read the pre-consumption array, both pass indexOf, and both be authenticated before either update lands, violating the documented 'each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee. Consumption must be atomic (e.g. conditional update/transaction) so only one request can claim a code.

Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

false_positives.candidate:
Disabling 2FA with a backup code has the same case-sensitivity bug

This endpoint computes backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '')) without lowercasing/trimming. A correctly transcribed backup code entered in uppercase therefore returns IncorrectBackupCode, so a user who has lost their authenticator cannot disable 2FA with a valid code. Normalize the input the same way codes are generated/stored before checking membership.

External IdP users in the totpEmail flow cannot reach the backup-code option

When totpEmail is present (the flow used for Google/SAML users who have 2FA enabled), the footer is ExternalTotpFooter, which only offers Cancel, instead of TwoFactorFooter which contains the 'Lost access' toggle. The BackupCode form is rendered only when twoFactorLostAccess becomes true, and that state can never be set in this flow, even though the credentials authorize callback now supports backupCode. External-IdP 2FA users who lost their authenticator therefore still have no backup-code login path.

The added e2e coverage only clicks the backup-code download/copy buttons and checks the filename/toast during setup; the file itself notes 'TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup'. The security-critical new behavior — valid backup code logs in, the same code cannot be reused, an invalid code is rejected, and a backup code can disable 2FA — is entirely untested, so regressions in next-auth-options.ts or disable.ts would not be caught.

If the user dismisses the dialog via the Dialog's onOpenChange path (X button, outside click, Escape) after the server has already set twoFactorEnabled=true, the parent/security page is never refreshed and resetState() is not run, leaving the UI showing 2FA as disabled (and stale secret/backup-code state in the modal) until a full reload. Setup returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled for anyone with twoFactorEnabled=true, and this PR adds no regenerate/view endpoint or settings action. All pre-existing 2FA users therefore have backupCodes=null forever unless they disable and re-enable 2FA; if they try a backup code at login they get MissingBackupCodes, whose message says 'Please generate them in your settings' even though no such settings action exists. The merged credential written at line 265 keeps the old expired `expires_in`, and `getToken` at line 278 checks `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(...).success && !isExpired(o365AuthCredentials.expires_in)`, so the credential is treated as permanently expired and refreshed on every call.

Salesforce refresh uses prisma without importing it

A leaked secret allows an attacker to overwrite any user's app credentials.

Under sync parsing `expires_in` is stripped from `newTokens`, so `Math.round(Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000)` evaluates to NaN and is stored as `key.expiry_date` at line 124, together with the placeholder refresh token from `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. Any attendee can add arbitrary guests to a booking

The authorization accepts anyone whose email appears in booking.attendees. The new UI is on the organizer's bookings page, so attendee access is an unnecessary privilege expansion; only the organizer and authorized team admins/owners should be able to modify the guest list.

Calendar is updated with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's

When the caller is a team admin/owner or another authorized user who is not the booking organizer, the calendar event is updated using the caller's credentials (or fails to find the organizer's calendar), even though the handler loads booking.user with credentials/destinationCalendar. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead.

When `sendTo` is falsy — e.g. `booking.smsReminderNumber` is null/missing for SMS_ATTENDEE, a permanently invalid case — or when the rendered message is empty, neither branch executes, so retryCount stays 0 and the reminder is re-selected by every cron invocation until its scheduledDate passes. The catch block now performs `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` without any nested try/catch. If that update fails — e.g. Prisma P2025 because the reminder was deleted concurrently by a booking cancellation/reschedule, or a transient DB error (which may be the same error that triggered the catch) — the exception propagates out of the for loop and out of the handler.
